name: DNA viewer
description: one DNA or RNA drawn at the level of detail that fits what is shown: a circular plasmid map, a linear map, both strands as sequence, or, zoomed in, the molecule itself as a ladder of phosphates, sugars and paired bases, with 5' and 3' ends, phosphates and sticky-end overhangs. Zoom, pan and jump to a feature are links
phrases: what does this fragment look like
zoom in on a region of a plasmid

requires.note: the render function: draws coordinates it is given, computes nothing

returns: markup for one DNA; performs no I/O
notes: Arguments are dna.layout's. A plasmid file: `show dna.view --arg file=test/fixtures/dna/pUC19.annotated.gb`. A region, to zoom in: add `--arg region=375..420`. A fragment C11 wants to explain: `show dna.view --arg sequence=GGTCTCAATGC --arg ext5=AATT --arg mod5=phos5 --arg mark='BsaI site=1..6'`. Over the transport the same thing is /view?id=dna.view&file=...&region=..., which is also what every link on the page is, so zooming asks the producer again rather than running anything in the page. Links work under `serve`; a page written once by `show --open` is a snapshot whose links do nothing.
